claims.text: Under POL-NS-23 the 5.00 SGD fee stands only if the driver both messaged and called before cancelling, and the message limb here is carried by a single artifact: the chat log EV-CHAT-05059 (the trip record's own contact block derives its message_count and obligation_met from that same id). That artifact is IMPAIRED — issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE, weight 0.85 — because MSG-05059-001 and MSG-05059-002 were delivered (08:29:31 and 08:32:47) but both carry read_at null, so the rider never opened either one. Under POL-GEN-02 the message limb cannot be credited at full weight and any confidence placed on it is capped at 0.85, so if the judge cannot treat that limb as established, POL-NS-23 voids the fee outright and the whole 5.00 SGD charged on EV-FARE-05059 is returned to the rider as a FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03.

The premise the whole charge rests on — that the rider was not at the pickup point — is established by nothing on this record. The only location evidence is the driver-device trace EV-GPS-05059, whose rider_track is empty, and the sole support for 'rider not on board' is the platform's own wait-timer expiry at 08:34:15 in EV-TRIP-05059, which is a clock event and not an observation of the rider. The third-party traffic artifact that could have corroborated conditions at the pickup was never attached (EV-ADVIS-05059-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, no payload). POL-GEN-26 requires escalation where a fact a rule needs cannot be established from the evidence that would carry it, and the occurrence of the no-show itself is that fact here; the case should go to a human reviewer with that open question stated, rather than the rider carrying the 5.00 SGD on a premise no artifact on file proves.

The rider's own contention that the driver 'cancelled too fast' cannot be sustained on this record and I do not press it: this was an on-demand trip, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 08:29:10 to 08:34:10, and the driver cancelled at 08:35:30 — 380 s after arrival and 80 s after the wait expired. The trip record and the GPS trace agree on both timestamps, so the timing limb of the rider's claim fails, and the rider's case stands on the notice limb alone.

On the one profile field the policy makes citable for this test, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 3 counting this trip if its fee stands, which under POL-NS-25 is a referral of the account for review and nothing more; the clause states that referral never changes the ruling on the trip, so the rider does not rely on it and it carries no weight either way in this decision.

claims.text: The free wait was served in full. This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled_at, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 08:29:10 and expired at 08:34:10; the driver did not cancel until 08:35:30, i.e. 380 s after arrival and roughly 80 s past the expiry of the free wait period. The trip record's own free_wait block marks cancelled_after_free_wait as true. On POL-NS-21 the cancellation fell inside the window in which the driver may cancel for a rider no-show.

The arrival that starts that wait is not merely the driver's word. The auto-arrival event at 08:29:10 is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace: from 08:29:05 the fixes sit stationary at the pickup, the nearest fix is 6.55 m from the pickup point against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and its reported accuracy of 3.0 m is inside the 25 m accuracy filter. That trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, with 100% coverage, 25 fixes at a 30 s interval and no gap longer than 30 s.

Both limbs of the POL-NS-23 contact obligation were met before cancellation. The driver sent MSG-05059-001 at 08:29:30 and MSG-05059-002 at 08:32:45, and placed an in-app call at 08:33:40 that rang 25 s unanswered — message and call, each before cancelled_at of 08:35:30. I disclose that the chat artifact is IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 on issue UNREAD_MESSAGE, but that impairment points the other way: POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have SENT a message and PLACED a call, not that the rider opened or answered either, and the delivery timestamps (08:29:31 and 08:32:47) confirm both messages reached the rider's device. No FULL_REFUND arises under POL-NS-23.

The rider's account is contradicted by the record rather than supported by it. The rider says the driver 'cancelled too fast' and that the rider 'did not even see his message'; the record shows 6 minutes 20 seconds of stationary waiting at the pickup, two delivered chat messages, and an unanswered 25 s in-app call before the cancellation at 08:35:30. That the messages carry no read_at is consistent with the rider not having opened them, which is the rider's own conduct during a wait the driver was entitled to end, and it is not a fact that voids the fee under POL-NS-21.

The fee charged is exactly the fee the policy sets, so nothing in POL-NS-22's amount check is engaged. The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy true, policy_fee_sgd 5.00 and payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. Under POL-NS-22 a driver who cancels after the free wait is entitled to that 5.00 SGD as compensation for time and fuel, and under POL-GEN-03 the outcome for a standing no-show fee is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee.

Nothing in the record excuses the rider's non-appearance. EV-ADVIS-05059-01, the traffic advisory for this trip, is MISSING: its admissibility status is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0, and under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact. There is therefore no item of evidence showing any external condition that kept the rider from the pickup or that would lengthen the wait the driver owed.

POL-GEN-26 is not engaged, so there is no open question to escalate. Every fact the no-show rules require is on the record: the arrival (08:29:10), the start and expiry of the free wait (08:29:10 to 08:34:10), the contact (two messages and one unanswered call), the cancellation (08:35:30) and the fee charged (5.00 SGD). In particular, the absence of a scheduled_at on this on-demand trip does not open a gap, because POL-NS-21 supplies the start of the wait for an on-demand trip — the driver's arrival — and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence except where a rule says so.

POL-NS-24 does not assist the rider either. That clause requires the driver to have failed to arrive at the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes; here the only arrival evidence is a verified arrival at 08:29:10, corroborated by the GPS trace, and the driver waited a further 6 minutes 20 seconds and attempted contact before cancelling. There was no arrival failure, and because a message and a call were both made there was no contact failure, so neither the full refund nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit that POL-NS-24 attaches to a contact failure is available on this record.

The AI ruling is final here, which removes any argument for holding this case open. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold at which the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider fraud_flags 0, driver fraud_flags 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 confidence bar is not raised; and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final subject to those bars. Nothing on this record brings the fee within a human-review band.

Because the fee stands, POL-NS-25's repeat no-show referral is triggered and should be recorded: rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is present and stands at 3, and the rule applies once that count reaches 3 or more. This is a referral naming POL-NS-25 only — it never changes the ruling on this trip, and I do not put it forward as a reason to decide anything.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. The rider filed this dispute, contesting the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-05059. On the record the fee stands, and the ruling moves that 5.00 SGD to the driver as compensation.

1. Timing (POL-NS-21). This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled pickup time, so the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival. The trip record and the driver-device GPS trace agree: arrival 08:29:10, free wait expiring 08:34:10, cancellation 08:35:30 — 380 seconds after arrival and about 80 seconds after the free wait expired, and the trip record's own free_wait block marks cancelled_after_free_wait true. The rider's contention that the driver 'cancelled too fast' is not supported on the record.

2. Arrival (POL-NS-21 arrival test). The auto-arrival at 08:29:10 is corroborated by the GPS trace: from 08:29:05 the fixes sit stationary at the pickup, the nearest fix is 6.55 m from the pickup point (inside the 50 m STANDARD radius) with a reported accuracy of 3.0 m (inside the 25 m filter). The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, 100% coverage, 25 fixes at 30 s, no gap over 30 s.

3. Contact obligation (POL-NS-23). The driver sent two in-app messages (08:29:30 and 08:32:45) and placed an in-app call (08:33:40, unanswered, rang 25 s), all before the 08:35:30 cancellation. The clause requires the driver to have SENT a message and PLACED a call, not that the rider read or answered. I therefore reject the rider's argument that the chat log voids the message limb: EV-CHAT-05059 is impaired at weight 0.85 on issue UNREAD_MESSAGE — the two messages were delivered (08:29:31 and 08:32:47) but carry no read_at — but that defect concerns whether the rider opened them, not whether the driver sent them, and delivery confirms both reached the rider's device. No FULL_REFUND arises under POL-NS-23.

4. Fee amount (POL-NS-22). The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total charged 5.00 SGD, refund_issued_sgd 0.0; the amount matches the policy fee, so POL-NS-22's amount check is not engaged and adds no referral.

5. Finality (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26). The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band at which the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0), so the 0.95 bar is not raised; no safety flag applies. No escalation is needed — every fact the no-show rules require (arrival, free wait, contact, cancellation, fee) is on the record, so POL-GEN-26 opens no question.

Because the fee stands, POL-NS-22 gives DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with the money the ruling moves (5.00 SGD) carried in both amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd. The 5.00 SGD fee figure is taken from EV-FARE-05059 (fee_charged_sgd 5.00, policy_fee_sgd 5.00).

Referral: POL-NS-25 flags the rider's account for review, the count being 3.

Confidence is set at 0.85: the deciding facts are carried by the trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown at weight 1.0, but the message limb of the contact obligation is carried by the chat log at weight 0.85 (impaired, UNREAD_MESSAGE), which caps confidence.
referrals: POL-NS-25: flag the rider's account for review — rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 3 counting this trip where its fee stands, at or above the 3-in-30-days threshold (mandatory upfront payment; temporary suspension pending Trust & Safety review). This referral rides with the ruling and does not change it.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: I have reviewed trip TRP-05059 and the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged on 27 Aug 2026, and the fee stands.

The rider's timing complaint does not hold. This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 08:29:10 to 08:34:10 (trip record EV-TRIP-05059, free_wait block). The rider's second point — that the fee should be voided because the driver's messages were never read — does not void it either. POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have SENT at least one in-app chat message AND PLACED at least one in-app call before cancelling; it does not require the rider to have read or answered either. The driver sent MSG-05059-001 at 08:29:30 and MSG-05059-002 at 08:32:45 and placed an in-app call at 08:33:40 that rang 25 s unanswered, all before the cancellation at 08:35:30 (trip record contact_before_cancel; chat log EV-CHAT-05059). I disclose that the chat log EV-CHAT-05059 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 on issue UNREAD_MESSAGE (both messages delivered, read_at null): that impairment is why my confidence is 0.85 rather than higher, because the message limb is carried by that artifact and its weight caps any confidence placed on it — but it does not change the outcome, because the clause tests sending, not reading.
